The vice president of vehicle hardware engineering at Ford, Charles Poon, explained, “Mistakenly, we thought that by just introducing artificial intelligence and adjusting the design requirements that we had, that that would produce a high-quality product.”

The firm saw that as experienced engineers left, they took a vast amount of institutional knowledge with them. Vital information was omitted from the datasets used to train AI systems. This has led Ford to bring back and promote over 350 experienced engineers to improve data collection and interpretation methods to support AI training for future applications. However, it remains unclear whether this will be effective.
